content.title: Women’s March Madness Selection Sunday live updates and reaction: UConn, UCLA, Texas, South Carolina grab No. 1 seeds in NCAA Tournament
content.text: Women's March Madness Ranking UConn 12 Championships Geno's Body Language Goliaths in Final Four Women's Bracket Forecast Women’s March Madness Selection Sunday live updates and reaction: UConn, UCLA, Texas, South Carolina grab No. 1 seeds in NCAA Tournament The women's NCAA Tournament bracket is set and ready for March Madness to begin The Athletic Live Team and more March 15, 2026 at 10:00 PM EDT UConn will face UTSA in the first round. Getty Images Daniel Shirley · Senior Editor, Live Field ready for women's March Madness The women’s NCAA Tournament bracket is set with defending champion UConn as the No. 1 overall seed. UCLA , Texas and South Carolina are the other No. 1 seeds. The games begin with the First Four on Wednesday and Thursday, followed by the first round on Friday and Saturday. Check out our printable bracket here . Share your thoughts on the NCAA field: live@theathletic.com GO FURTHER UConn, UCLA, Texas and South Carolina earn No. 1 seeds in women’s NCAA Tournament March 15, 2026 at 10:00 PM EDT Michael Waterloo Bracket breakdown: Texas Longhorns Pluses : Rori Harmon is the pulse of Texas basketball, as the returning senior leads a trio of standouts (junior Madison Booker and sophomore Jordan Lee ). Texas is gifted offensively, but its defense makes the Longhorns stand out. They play a suffocating full-court press off a make, regularly forcing opponents in half-court violations, inbounds violations, and turnovers in the entry zone. Their defense holds opponents to less than 57 points per game and has the nation's second-best defensive rating. Minuses : If Lee has an off game, who is going to fill that No. 3 void? Booker will get hers in the midrange, but Texas, which struggles behind the arc, counts on Lee and freshman Aaliyah Crump to space the floor and hit the deep shot. Texas’ bench is thin behind Crump, Kyla Oldacre and Bryanna Preston , so it needs all three stars clicking at the same time to play to its full potential. Projection : Texas suffered back-to-back losses to LSU and South Carolina by a combined eight points in conference play, but it defeated both in separate matchups during the season. When Texas is in rhythm, there’s not a team it can’t beat. Its defensive pressure and effectiveness interrupting the passing lanes will keep it in games, but it needs Lee and Crump to pose as threats behind the arc. Schaefer’s team is near the bottom of all Division I teams in attempted 3s again this season. But Texas can win it all and send Harmon out on top. March 15, 2026 at 9:55 PM EDT Michael Waterloo Bracket breakdown: South Carolina Gamecocks Pluses : South Carolina came up short in last season's title game against UConn. Despite not having MiLaysia Fulwiley, Te-Hina Paopao, Chloe Kitts and other key members of last season’s team, South Carolina is back toward the top. The Gamecocks' success comes from balanced scoring — led by super sophomore Joyce Edwards — but their defensive effort is also strong. South Carolina holds opponents to less than than 58 points per game. The Gamecocks are unselfish, averaging 18.1 assists per game. Minuses : South Carolina is efficient from behind the arc, shooting nearly 38 percent on 3-pointers, but it averages just 16.5 3-point attempts per game. Without Paopao around anymore, it has counted on Florida State transfer Ta’Niya Latson and Tessa Johnson as outside threats. In its November loss to Texas, South Carolina made just two 3-pointers — its second-lowest mark all season. Projection : Betting against Dawn Staley in March Madness is like betting against A’ja Wilson in the WNBA — both at your own risk. South Carolina may not be as polished as its past rosters, but with Raven Johnson ’s offensive development, Latson finding her offensive groove, and freshman Alicia Tournebize becoming more acclimated and comfortable after her late (early?) start with the team, the Gamecocks can go toe-to-toe with any team and make another deep run. March 15, 2026 at 9:50 PM EDT Michael Waterloo Bracket breakdown: Vanderbilt Commodores Getty Images Pluses : This is a special team. It’s averaging its most points per game in school history, and it has its most regular-season wins in 20 years. Mikayla Blakes is the truest scorer in the country, but she’s not doing it alone. Aubrey Galvan , Justine Pissott and Sacha Washington complement Blakes extremely well. Shea Ralph coaches the Commodores to compete with anyone with its explosive offense and efficiency from all three levels. Minuses : Rebound the ball. Just rebound the ball on the defensive side. That’s been the glaring weakness. Out of 363 DI teams, Vanderbilt ranks No. 318 in the category. In losses, it was outrebounded by an average of 7.6 boards. Projection : With a player of Blakes’ caliber, the ceiling is the championship game. That’s how pure of a bucket she is. There are warts, but if the offense can score to its potential, the floor is the ceiling for Vanderbilt. Anything less than the Sweet 16 would be a disappointment, but an Elite Eight appearance at least is the expectation. March 15, 2026 at 9:45 PM EDT Michael Waterloo Bracket breakdown: Iowa Hawkeyes Getty Images Pluses : Iowa quietly has a big three in Chit-Chat Wright , Hannah Stuelke and Ava Heiden . The trio leads a high-scoring attack, thanks to Wright’s explosiveness and Stuelke’s dominance in the paint. What’s most impressive is that Iowa had one of the nation's hardest schedules, and despite a three-game losing streak, it righted the ship to end the regular season with a key victory against Michigan. Minuses : As good as Iowa is at facilitating offensively and handling defensive rebounds, it struggles to generate second-chance opportunities on the offensive glass. The bigger issue defensively is allowing opponents to effectively shoot at a high rate from behind the arc. In its five regular-season losses, opponents shot 47.3 percent on 3-pointers. Projection : Expectations are high for Iowa once again. It showed that it can hang with anyone not named UCLA or UConn, which bodes well for at least a Sweet 16 appearance for Jan Jensen in Year 2. March 15, 2026 at 9:40 PM EDT Michael Waterloo Bracket breakdown: UCLA Bruins Getty Images Pluses : It’s pick your poison when it comes to the Bruins, as they have five first-round talents in their starting lineup. Lauren Betts gets the attention – as she should – but Utah transfer Gianna Kneepkens offers the spacing UCLA needs as a sharpshooter from 3-point range. Add to that Gabriela Jaquez ’s breakout performance this season freeing up Kiki Rice , the elite defense that UCLA plays, and this could be the year that UCLA gets to the title game. Minuses: Is it a copout to say none? We can highlight the same issue that UCLA had last season entering the tournament, which is its free-throw rate. For an offensively stacked team, it doesn’t get to the line often at all. UCLA is shooting nearly 80 percent from the charity stripe, so it is converting, but free throws can be the difference during March Madness. Just ask Jaquez, whose misses at the end of the game against Michigan nearly cost the Bruins. Projection : If there’s ever a season for UCLA to win the national title, it’s this one. The Bruins lost to Texas by 11 earlier in the season, but they have steamrolled the rest of its competition during the regular season. This is the most complete team that Cori Close has had at UCLA, leading the nation in points per 100 possessions. Saying championship-or-bust isn’t fair, but anything less than an appearance in the Final Four will be a disappointment. March 15, 2026 at 9:36 PM EDT Michael Waterloo Bracket breakdown: Michigan Wolverines Getty Images Pluses : Growth isn’t always linear, but in the case of Michigan, it seems to be. Olivia Olson , Mila Holloway and Syla Swords are back with two full regular seasons under their belts, and it shows. Olson looks like a future WNBA first-round pick, and Swords can hit a shot from anywhere on the court with a quick release. The key player may be Brooke Quarles Daniels , who is the best defensive stopper on the roster. Minuses : Michigan is still undergoing a few growing pains. It can get into foul trouble too often – especially with Quarles Daniels and Holloway. The guards and wings are great at crashing the offensive glass, but its lack of a dominant interior becomes an issue when teams with inside strength getting second-chance opportunities off the boards. Shooting less than 68 percent on free throws also doesn’t get the job done. Projection : The game of the year came in November. It was UConn against Michigan, and UConn escaped with a three-point win. But Michigan arguably got more out of that loss than UConn with the win. The Wolverines showed they can compete with the best. It’ll be hard to pick against Michigan making the Elite Eight and maybe even the Final Four. It may be a season too early, but the Wolverines are building toward something special. March 15, 2026 at 9:32 PM EDT The Athletic Live Team 'No Offseason' breaks down the bracket Our first-ever "No Offseason" Selection Sunday livestream is happening now! Come break down the bracket with our experts at The Athletic. March 15, 2026 at 9:30 PM EDT Michael Waterloo Bracket breakdown: LSU Tigers Getty Images Pluses : LSU is going to score buckets. We know this already. Kim Mulkey’s team will push the pace and constantly look to score in transition. Six Tigers average more than nine points per game, with Flau’jae Johnson leading the charge. The senior returned to LSU for an additional season, looking to hone her 3-point shooting. She’s done just that for the Tigers, shooting a career high behind the arc. Minuses : “It’s not that LSU struggles from behind the arc — it’s just that it gets most of its shot attempts up from 2-point range.” That’s what was written here about LSU last year, and the same remains true this year. The Tigers are toward the nation's bottom in 3-point attempts, doing most of their work inside the arc. Given their fast pace, though, it results in a lot of iso-ball situations where they play too fast and don’t get into their motions before getting up a shot. In 11 games, the Tigers dished 15 or fewer assists, and they lost four of those contests. Projection : Johnson, MiLaysia Fulwiley and Mikaylah Williams lead the charge for LSU, but it's a team that runs deeper than it seems on the surface. Freshman Grace Knox has played a larger-than-expected role, as has transfer Amiya Joyner . LSU's offense can carry it to Phoenix, but it has to know when to settle down offensively instead of forcing up bad shots early in the shot clock. Few teams can keep pace with LSU on the floor, so expect at least an Elite Eight run. March 15, 2026 at 9:25 PM EDT Michael Waterloo Bracket breakdown: UConn Huskies Getty Images Pluses : The Big East isn’t what it used to be, but UConn scheduled nine Power 4 games this year, and only Michigan kept it within single digits. It’s a team that is not defined by its conference, but rather by its depth even after losing Paige Bueckers to the WNBA. Sarah Strong looks every part of being a Player of the Year, while Azzi Fudd is showing that she can run the offense by facilitating or hitting her soft jumper. On any given night, UConn can turn to Ashlynn Shade , KK Arnold , Blanca Quinonez , Serah Williams or Kayleigh Heckel as the third offensive option to complement its nation-leading scoring defense. Minuses : The only real concern with UConn is the number of 3-pointers opponents take. Of course, it has to do with UConn’s interior defense and teams playing catch up, but if the Huskies run into a hot team on the wrong day, it could prove problematic. We are searching for a needle in a haystack here, OK? This team truly has no weakness. Projection : UConn showed that it can compete with anyone outside the Big East. Scheduling an early February game against Tennessee after a strong early nonconference schedule was a great way to stay ready for the top-level action it will face in the NCAA Tournament. UConn is the undisputed favorite to repeat as champions, and anything less than a Final Four appearance in Phoenix won’t just be a disappointment, it will be shocking. March 15, 2026 at 9:20 PM EDT Michael Charles · Staff Writer, Live While there was some debate and consternation about the No. 1 overall seed in the women's NCAA Tournament, UConn ultimately got the nod. Subscriber Terence T. believes this was the correct decision. T Terence T. · Mar 16 I can see where it might have been close between UCONN and UCLA, but when the only undefeated team is the defending national champion, it would be pretty hard to not name them overall number one. 33 4 March 15, 2026 at 8:12 PM EDT Sabreena Merchant · Staff Writer, Women's Basketball UConn, UCLA, Texas and South Carolina earn No. 1 seeds in women’s NCAA Tournament For the 15th time in program history, UConn is the No. 1 overall seed in the NCAA Tournament. The Huskies earned the honor after an undefeated 31-0 regular season — their 11th in program history — and three more Big East tournament wins en route to a conference title. UConn is looking to become the first repeat champion since the Huskies accomplished the feat in 2015-16 as part of a four-year championship dynasty. As expected, UConn was joined as a No. 1 seed by UCLA, Texas and South Carolina. Full Story March 15, 2026 at 9:10 PM EDT Michael Charles · Staff Writer, Live What is the metric wins above bubble (WAB)? NCAA selection committee chair Amanda Braun explains with insights on how a balanced bracket is created: “We have technology tools that add up the seed, the true seed, for each of the teams in each of those pods. In that first four lines, we aim to have a differential of the highest and lowest numbers, when you tally those four seed line columns, to be no more than five, and this year we achieved three, which is tells you that it's a very balanced bracket, and we're really proud of that work.” March 15, 2026 at 9:06 PM EDT Michael Charles · Staff Writer, Live Amanda Braun also discussed the committee's decision to seed Minnesota just above Maryland: “Both Minnesota and Maryland had wonderful seasons, and Minnesota had the edge on on the metrics, with the net, the WAB and strength of schedule. Really, that as a whole, had an edge there and Minnesota down the stretch playing just a little bit stronger than Maryland in the last 10 games or so.” March 15, 2026 at 9:02 PM EDT Grace Raynor · Staff Writer, Recruiting Dumb question: Is "observable component" just a fancy way of saying the eye test? March 15, 2026 at 9:00 PM EDT John Riker · Staff Writer, Live South Carolina celebrates after securing a top seed Getty Images Perennial power South Carolina did not win the SEC Championship this year, but it is well-positioned to chase the even more ambitious goal of an NCAA championship. That road starts in Columbia thanks to South Carolina's 31-3 record, and the Gamecocks were thrilled to lead the Sacramento region. IT'S OFFICIALLY MARCH, AND IT'S TIME TO DANCE 💃 pic.twitter.com/hWPDl1Zz18 — South Carolina Women's Basketball (@GamecockWBB) March 16, 2026 March 15, 2026 at 8:58 PM EDT Michael Charles · Staff Writer, Live Let's hear from the NCAA selection committee chair Getty Images Amanda Braun, the athletic director at the University of Milwaukee Wisconsin, served as this year's NCAA selection committee chair. She spoke with Holly Rowe on ESPN's Selection Sunday show, first speaking about why the committee chose to award UConn the No. 1 overall seed: 💬 “I would say the observable component was talked about a whole lot the way we watched UConn win and win throughout the year, from the beginning to the end. UCLA did a lot of winning as well. But, ultimately, the committee felt like the observable component with UConn really gave them the edge.” March 15, 2026 at 8:51 PM EDT Michael Waterloo Women’s March Madness bracket prep: Strengths, weaknesses for all 68 teams, outlooks and more For most of the season, the No. 1 seeds left no doubt who they would be on Selection Sunday. UConn with its undefeated dominance and UCLA with its senior-led class of talent are the class of the tournament. But you never count out South Carolina, and Texas has shown it can win big games. But after those four? The order had been up for debate all season long. Full Story March 15, 2026 at 8:50 PM EDT Michael Charles · Staff Writer, Live The full bracket is now set! The Bracket. 🔗 https://t.co/BTd0jTculb 🎟️ https://t.co/uinvwwRlnm 📲 https://t.co/G2KeqiVWZ3 #MarchMadness pic.twitter.com/B2EL223z0D — NCAA March Madness (@MarchMadnessWBB) March 16, 2026 March 15, 2026 at 8:47 PM EDT Scott Dochterman · Staff Writer, Big Ten Getty Images It makes sense for Iowa to play on Saturday and potentially Monday. The Hawkeyes still garner among the highest television ratings nationally and the Nielsen ratings leaves out BTN. If it's Iowa-South Carolina in the Elite 8, that will mark the third time in the last four years the schools will have met in the Elite 8, Final Four or national championship.
